Excellent! The white precipitate (AgCl) completely dissolved in excess ammonia. This is the definitive confirmatory test for Ag⁺. 

The dissolution occurs because AgCl reacts with ammonia to form the soluble diamminesilver(I) complex:
AgCl(s) + 2NH₃(aq) → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

This behavior is characteristic and specific to silver chloride among common metal chlorides, confirming that the cation is indeed **Ag⁺**.

Final Answer: Ag+
